headline: Recommended filing a resolution encouraging residents to gather signatures for a City Charter review, which the committee did not advance.
summary: Members discussed how a Charter Commission could be created, including the 15% registered voter signature requirement and non-binding ballot questions. Members voted to recommend filing a Chairman's Resolution that encourages residents to gather those signatures. Members also voted to recommend filing five informational communications about Charter changes.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 15, 2026 meeting by a 2-0 roll call vote, with Bergman absent.
Recommended filing the Chairman's Resolution encouraging residents to gather signatures of 15% of registered voters to request a City Charter review, by a 3-0 roll call vote.
Recommended filing Items 4a through 4e, informational communications on Charter changes, ballot questions, meeting advertisements, and resident testimony, by a 3-0 roll call vote.

September 28, 2026 Page 2 of 7Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Order of Councilor Gary Rosen, Councilor Morris A. Bergman, Councilor Robert A . 
Bilotta, Councilor Tony Economou, Councilor John P. Fresolo, Councilor Khrystian E . 
King, Councilor Satya B. Mitra, Councilor Luis A. Ojeda, Councilor Jose A. Rivera, 
Councilor Kathleen M. Toomey and Mayor Joseph M. Petty - Request Standing 
Committee on Municipal and Legislative Operations hold a public hearing to determine 
the feasibility and advisability of the City Council initiating and /or supporting efforts to 
review the current modified Plan E City Charter, which was implemented in 1987 and 
amended in 2022.
# 9k CC February 3, 2026
a.
In Committee May 20, 2026 - Held
In Committee August 17, 2026 - Held
September 28, 2026 Page 3 of 7Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Chairperson Councilor Mitra read the item and recognized the following Speakers:
1. Fred Nathan, Worcester resident, spoke in opposition to a charter review
2. Gordon Davis, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
3. Gary Hunter, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
4. Tom Marino, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
5. David Webb, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
6. Francesco Bivona, Worcester resident, spoke neither in favor nor opposed to a charter review.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed the importance of using 
the ALERTWorcester system to notify the public of the committee meetings, his belief that a 
Charter Commission would benefit the city, and the process required to establish a Charter 
Commission.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed why a Charter 
Commission has not existed since 1985, as well as the importance of establishing a Charter 
Commission through the means of obtaining signatures from fifteen percent (15%) of the city’s 
registered voters.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized the City Clerk, who provided a presentation concerning 
the requirements associated with establishing a Charter Commission for a Charter Review.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the ballot question to 
create a Charter Commission in 1983, the requirements for Charter Commissioners and whether a 
candidate for the City Council can also be a candidate for the Charter Commission with the City 
Clerk and the City Solicitor.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed the Charter Revision or 
Adoption Petition form, the number of candidates for Charter Commissioners and that a Charter 
Commission can only be established through the ballot process.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra discussed the requirement of obtaining signatures of fifteen percent 
(15%) of the city’s registered voters using Charter Revision or Adoption Petition form, as well as 
the types of charter changes that can occur from a Charter Commission with the City Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the requirement for 
the number of signatures for a Charter Commissioner candidate with the City Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra then discussed the role of the Charter Commissioners with the City 
Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed the process related to 
establishing a Charter Commission.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the importance of 
having a democratic process for Charter Change.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Speaker #3, who spoke concerning the item.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Speaker #4, who discussed the non -binding questions on 
the 1991 ballot with the City Clerk.
September 28, 2026 Page 4 of 7Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed the results of the 
non-binding questions regarding Charter Change on the 1991 Municipal Election ballot with the 
City Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the potential for 
negative consequences associated with placing a non -binding question on the ballot, as well as the 
required to place a non-binding question on ballot with the City Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed the deadline for the 
submission of the signatures for Charter Revision or Adoption Petition form with the City Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra discussed the process and timeline related to placing a non -binding 
question on ballot with the City Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra then discussed complications associated with forth a Chairman’s 
Resolution to City Council regarding encouraging the efforts of the members of the public to 
obtain the required signatures to establish a Charter Commission to review the City Charter with 
Councilor Rosen and Councilor Bergman. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized the Deputy City Clerk, who discussed the language 
concerning the Chairman’s Resolution with Councilor Rosen.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra brought forth the following Chairman’s Resolution: “That the City 
Council does hereby encourage the efforts of members of the public to get the signatures of fifteen 
percent (15%) of the city’s registered voters to request that the City of Worcester review and /or 
revise its present Charter, or to adopt a new Charter."
Chairperson Councilor Mitra moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be filed.
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
